mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (prev value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's mean (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified rising rate window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 10,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns show no significant outperformance versus a 30-day moving average baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% indicates weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (prev month - 2%) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns (aligned to 5-day window) are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, supply-side pressures are inferred, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) relative to a 30-day moving average during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified tightening period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in retail sales proxy (HOUST) of at least 5% suggest resilient demand, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > (prev month + 5%) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant outperformance versus a 30-day rolling average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxy (implied via interaction of multiple demand/supply series) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: Dual contraction in supply and demand
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in line with expected contraction patterns.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary policy easing regime (as inferred from FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are expected to be positive due to lower borrowing costs and increased investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified easing regime.
